newsitem.title: GERMANY: BAe, Mannesmann in running for STN Atlas.
newsitem.headline: BAe, Mannesmann in running for STN Atlas.

text.p: Negotiations to sell bankrupt Bremer Vulkan's STN Atlas Elektronik defence unit are in their final stages, with one British and two German groups in the running, Bremen radio said late on Thursday.

The German consortiums are headed by Mannesmann AG and Diehl, while British Aerospace is also interested in buying out STN Atlas -- the bankrupt north German shipbuilding group's only profitable unit.
The radio said British Aerospace had made a "financially interesting" offer, and company officials had been in Bremen this week to take a closer look at the company.
Bremer Vulkan's collapse revealed that European Union (EU) subsidies had been channelled from the former communist east to -- unsuccessfully -- prop up its west German shipyards.
EU competition commissioner Karel Van Miert told Radio Bremen that subsidies would continue to be paid to east German shipyards if western shipbuilding capacity was sharply reduced.
But, he said, he had not been told of any plans to do so.
The European Court has ruled that subsidies granted in 1993 by the city of Bremen to buy STN's predecessor Krupp Atlas Elektronik would not have to be repaid.
